notes: Reference propellant for essentially all flown gridded-ion and Hall thrusters. Scarce and expensive; produced as an air-separation by-product

Cheaper and more abundant than xenon and lighter, so a higher Isp at the same discharge potential. Harder to ionise, which is why the gain is not realised in practice. Stored density at 14 MPa and 50 C is about one third that of xenon (S12). Measured operating points are in the thrusters table: spt100_kr_390v, spt100_kr_nom and bht1500c_kr, each with a matched xenon control
VASIMR VX-200 benchmark propellant (S15). Lowest cost, hardest to ionise of the noble gases in use
Molar mass is that of the accelerated atomic ion; stored as solid I2 (253.808 g/mol) and sublimated. Removes the high-pressure tank. Chemically aggressive toward spacecraft materials

Lowest first ionisation energy in use, which is why AF-MPD efficiency is highest on lithium (S13). Condensable, so plume contamination is a vehicle-level problem. Requires a vaporiser whose power is usually excluded from quoted efficiencies

NTP propellant. Lowest molar mass gives the highest Isp at a given core temperature. Must be held at 20 K for up to 18 months for a Mars architecture; passive boil-off of order 16 t/yr on a 38 t tank (S21)
